principles: Local proof controls must be mechanical and deterministic, not prose-only.
PINN domain support must never imply PDE correctness, solver quality, production readiness, or external Authority completion.
Schema, adapters, gate decisions, benchmark metrics, and report wording must share one runtime model to avoid drift.
Failure modes must fail closed with stable reason codes and visible remediation.
Verification must be runnable from the story worktree and bind to current source.
drivers: The user asked for all M0-M5 milestones to become DONE, not just documented.
Existing Proofbound command and policy registries require explicit CLI catalog and ownership entries for new commands.
The plan requires A1-A4/B1-B15 deterministic benchmark comparison and bounded governance wording.

options.name: docs-only hardening
cons: Would repeat B-2769 and fail the user request for runtime DONE
Cannot mechanically detect stale or mismatched evidence

options.name: large scientific PINN implementation
pros: Could run real PDE/PINN experiments eventually
Might be closer to research workflow tooling
cons: Would risk false PDE correctness claims
Too broad for Proofbound claim-control layer

options.name: bounded local runtime claim-control pack
pros: Directly implements schema, adapters, gate, benchmark, and report contracts
cons: Benchmark uses deterministic control fixtures rather than real PINN training
Future scientific integrations still need separate stories

rationale: This is the smallest honest implementation that makes M0-M5 executable while preserving the plan boundary and Proofbound local assurance rules.

preMortem.scenario: Generated commands accidentally imply PDE correctness or production readiness.
preMortem.trigger: Report wording or JSON fields expose productionDone=true, authorityDone=true, or PDE-correctness language.
preMortem.consequence: Users could overclaim scientific or production proof from a local diagnostic pack.
preMortem.mitigation: Hard-code productionDone=false/authorityDone=false, include boundary paragraph in all reports, and test wording/JSON adversarially.

preMortem.scenario: Schema accepts stale or mismatched evidence because only adapter pass status is checked.
preMortem.trigger: A receipt has exitCode=0 but carries a changed pdeSpecHash, grid hash, verifier hash, checkpoint hash, or output digest.
preMortem.consequence: Unsupported PINN claim advancement would still occur despite the domain pack.
preMortem.mitigation: Evaluate identity binding before adapter pass, require claim-specific identity fields, and pin B1-B15 injection tests to stable reason codes.

preMortem.scenario: Benchmark is gamed by making A4 perfect but hiding overhead or false stops.
preMortem.trigger: Harness reports only pass/fail counts and omits wall-time, intervention, repair/degrade/stop, or confidence intervals.
preMortem.consequence: The result overstates claim-control quality and violates the plan success criteria.
preMortem.mitigation: Benchmark report includes unsupported-advance, stale acceptance, boundary violation, reproducibility, false-stop, repair, intervention, overhead, and Wilson intervals.

preMortem.scenario: CLI integration drifts from registry or command policy.
preMortem.trigger: Handler exists but command catalog or ownership policy lacks the new command, causing help/owner gates/build checks to fail.
preMortem.consequence: The feature works only through imports, not as a user-visible Proofbound command.
preMortem.mitigation: Add command-catalog schemas, command policies, registry wiring, package scripts, smoke coverage, and build verification.
